metadata.title: SmartBrew requirements revised using student review
sources: Student decisions and justifications supplied in the conversation
Student clarification approving comparison row 5 and accepting row 7, including their supplied justifications.

Student instruction to fix the remaining review issues: retain ingredient display and saved-recipe deletion, correct source attribution and waste-reset justification, document the overflow proposal, and standardize decision labels.
metadata.scope: Reviewed full-system requirements artifact. This does not change or expand the separately implemented ten-function classroom prototype.

decision_rules.accept: Keep the AI suggestion, including an accepted omission.
decision_rules.reject: Reject the compared AI addition, reduction or omission; restore the baseline facet when applicable.
decision_rules.modify: Revise the AI requirement according to the student explanation and propagate changes to related constraints, stories and backlog items.
decision_rules.blank: Retain AI wording provisionally and mark the comparison facet as not reviewed; do not infer student approval.
decision_rules.unlisted_facets: Retain AI content unless a reviewed decision requires a consistency change.

metadata.identifier_policy: Existing FR, NFR and US identifiers are preserved; rejected items leave gaps. FR-25 adds disposal registration. PB-R01 through PB-R18 are revised backlog IDs, distinct from both source backlogs; source_backlog_ids provides explicit mapping.
metadata.planning_policy: PB-R01 through PB-R13 retain the exact numeric importance and estimate of baseline B1 through B13. These are historical planning values, not newly validated estimates of the expanded scope. Estimate units and importance-scale semantics remain undefined. New items have null values pending student/team estimation. Categorical must labels describe scope, not numeric business rank.

functional_requirements.name: Account creation
functional_requirements.description: Allow a user to create a personal SmartBrew account using a username and personal PIN; reject a username that is already taken.
preconditions: The user supplies a username and personal PIN.
For successful registration, the username is not already taken.
postconditions: Successful registration creates a personal account with the supplied username and PIN credentials.
A duplicate username does not create another account.

functional_requirements.name: User authentication
functional_requirements.description: Allow users to log in using their username and personal PIN or an associated NFC/card tap and access their own profile.
inputs: Username and personal PIN, or an associated NFC/card identifier
outputs: Access to the authenticated profile on success
preconditions: A matching account exists.
For card authentication, the presented identifier is associated with an account.
postconditions: Valid authentication gives access to the associated profile.
Invalid authentication does not grant profile access.
Logging out ends access to the authenticated profile until authentication succeeds again.

functional_requirements.name: Personal preference profiles
functional_requirements.description: Allow authenticated users to view and maintain their personal beverage preferences.
preconditions: The user is authenticated.
postconditions: Saved preference changes belong to the authenticated user's profile.

functional_requirements.name: Touchscreen menu, prices and beverage information
functional_requirements.description: Provide touchscreen navigation through beverage categories, show beverage prices, and allow inspection of the selected beverage nutritional and ingredient information.
outputs: Beverage category and menu views with prices
Nutritional information for the selected beverage
Ingredient information for the selected beverage
preconditions: The beverage catalogue, prices, nutritional data and ingredient information are configured.
postconditions: Users can see beverage prices while browsing.
Selecting a beverage allows users to inspect its nutritional values.
Inspecting a beverage allows users to view its ingredient information.

functional_requirements.name: Interactive beverage customization
functional_requirements.description: Allow users to customize supported recipe parameters, including milk type, coffee strength, temperature, and syrup shots, and reflect changes in the current recipe while they interact.
preconditions: A beverage has been selected.
The requested parameter values are supported by the machine.
postconditions: The current recipe reflects the accepted customization values.

functional_requirements.name: Named personal recipes
functional_requirements.description: Allow authenticated users to save, name, modify and delete custom beverage recipes in their profile, and select a saved recipe for one-touch ordering.
inputs: Save, modify, delete or order request
outputs: Order selection using the saved recipe
preconditions: The user is authenticated.
Modification or ordering requires an existing saved recipe.
Deletion requires an existing recipe belonging to the authenticated user.
postconditions: Saved changes are associated with the user's profile.
Selecting a saved recipe for ordering uses its stored customization values, subject to availability checks.
A successfully deleted recipe is removed from the user’s saved recipes and cannot be selected for future orders.

functional_requirements.name: Ingredient availability guard
functional_requirements.description: Prevent selection of a beverage when an ingredient it requires is depleted or below its configured minimum threshold.
outputs: Allowed selection or unavailable beverage indication
preconditions: Ingredient levels and minimum thresholds are available to the system.
postconditions: A beverage requiring a depleted or below-threshold ingredient cannot become a valid order selection.

functional_requirements.name: Beverage order execution
functional_requirements.description: Accept an available selected recipe as an order and coordinate payment and beverage preparation for that order.
outputs: Preparation instruction when the order is eligible to proceed
Confirmed order and calculated amount ready for payment
preconditions: The recipe passes ingredient availability checks.
Machine safety conditions allow preparation.
Payment acceptance follows the agreed online or offline policy.
postconditions: An eligible accepted order is submitted for preparation using its selected recipe.
An order blocked by payment or machine safety does not start preparation.
Before payment processing, the user has confirmed the order and the payable amount has been calculated.

functional_requirements.name: Supported payment methods
functional_requirements.description: Support payment through credit/debit EMV chip and contactless cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and internal prepaid employee cards.
inputs: Payment processor or employee card result
preconditions: The user has confirmed the order.
The amount to be paid has been calculated.
An order is awaiting payment.
The relevant reader and payment integration are configured.
postconditions: The order receives the payment outcome for the method used.
A rejected payment is not reported as accepted.

functional_requirements.name: Completed transaction history
functional_requirements.description: Automatically record every completed transaction, including the beverage customization parameters used, and associate it with the user's history when an authenticated user is identified.
preconditions: A transaction has reached the agreed completed state.
postconditions: The completed transaction and its customization values are available in transaction history.

functional_requirements.name: Digital receipts
functional_requirements.description: Offer a receipt for a completed transaction through a QR code scan or email, according to the user's choice.
inputs: Email address when email is selected
outputs: QR code providing receipt access or email receipt delivery result
preconditions: A completed transaction is available.
The selected delivery channel is available.
postconditions: The offered receipt corresponds to the completed transaction.
The selected delivery channel provides receipt access or reports its delivery outcome.

functional_requirements.name: Contextual drink recommendations
functional_requirements.description: Generate personalized recommendations for logged-in users using their locally available preferences and history, time of day, and available weather/context data. Missing external context degrades the recommendation calculation rather than disabling it.
outputs: Recommended drinks with calculated recommendation scores
preconditions: The user is logged in.
The local recommendation calculation and beverage options remain available.
postconditions: Recommendation scores use the authenticated user context and the specified inputs that remain available.
Unavailable weather or other external context does not disable the locally available recommendation calculation.
Users who are not logged in do not receive personalized recommendations.
Manual ordering remains available independently of recommendation or external-service availability.

functional_requirements.name: Mood-informed recipe suggestions
functional_requirements.description: Use the embedded camera to infer facial expression or mood and incorporate the inferred cue into tailored drink recipe suggestions.
preconditions: The user is logged in before receiving personalized mood-informed suggestions.
The camera is available.
Mood analysis operates under the agreed user permission policy.
postconditions: A successfully inferred mood cue is supplied to the suggestion calculation.
Captured facial images are handled according to NFR-01.

functional_requirements.name: Recommendation-based menu presentation
functional_requirements.description: Reorder and highlight touchscreen menu items according to calculated recommendation scores.
outputs: Reordered menu with highlighted recommended items
preconditions: The user is logged in before personalized menu ordering and highlighting are applied.
Recommendation scores have been calculated for menu items.
postconditions: Menu ordering and highlighting reflect the configured score presentation rule.

functional_requirements.name: Protected maintenance access
functional_requirements.description: Provide an administrative mode reserved for maintenance personnel, accessible through a physical key, NFC master card, or technician PIN.
inputs: Physical key state, NFC master card, or technician PIN
preconditions: Maintenance authentication mechanisms are configured.
postconditions: Successful maintenance authentication grants administrative access.
Unsuccessful authentication does not grant administrative access.
Maintenance logout revokes administrative access; subsequent users must authenticate separately before accessing administrative controls or protected diagnostic data.

functional_requirements.name: Ingredient refill registration
functional_requirements.description: Allow maintenance personnel to register physical ingredient refills, including milk, beans, cocoa, and cups, and reset the corresponding counters to configured maximum capacity.
preconditions: The operator has administrative access.
The corresponding ingredient has been physically refilled to maximum capacity.
postconditions: The selected ingredient counter equals its configured maximum capacity.

functional_requirements.name: Waste capacity monitoring and alerts
functional_requirements.description: Monitor liquid waste and coffee ground bin levels against capacity and alert maintenance personnel when disposal or emptying is required.
inputs: Configured bin capacities and alert thresholds
preconditions: Bin levels and configured capacities are available.
postconditions: A bin reaching its configured disposal threshold produces a corresponding technician alert.

functional_requirements.name: Bin-dependent overflow interlock
functional_requirements.description: Halt or block preparation operations that use, discharge into, or otherwise depend on an overflowing waste bin. Other drinks may proceed only when their preparation is verified to be independent of the affected bin and all other safety and ingredient checks pass.
inputs: Overflow status for each monitored bin
Current or requested recipe and its preparation steps
outputs: Halt or block instruction for affected preparation
Eligibility result for demonstrably unaffected recipes
preconditions: An overflow is detected in a monitored bin.
Dependencies between preparation operations and waste bins are configured and verified before allowing any exception.
postconditions: Preparation that depends on an overflowing bin does not start or continue while that overflow is active.
A drink may proceed only if all of its preparation operations are verified independent of overflowing bins and all other guards pass.
Unknown or unverified dependencies do not allow continued preparation.
Registering disposal does not by itself override an active overflow detection or another machine fault.

functional_requirements.name: Administrative error reporting
functional_requirements.description: Display current machine error messages on the administrative dashboard, including grinder jams, water heater faults, and low ingredient threshold conditions.
inputs: Machine fault and low ingredient events
preconditions: The machine reports an error condition.
The dashboard is accessible to authorized personnel.
postconditions: The dashboard identifies the reported error condition.

functional_requirements.name: Diagnostic event logs
functional_requirements.description: Record machine error events in event logs that support remote diagnostics.
outputs: Log access for authorized remote diagnostics when connected
preconditions: An error event has been reported.
postconditions: The reported error is represented in the diagnostic log without retaining facial images.

functional_requirements.name: Manual ordering during service outages
functional_requirements.description: When the network or an external service fails, retain basic manual beverage selection and customization using locally available machine functions and data.
inputs: Network or external service failure status
preconditions: The touchscreen, local control system, and required local menu data remain operational.
postconditions: Users can manually select an available beverage without a functioning weather or recommendation service.
Payment and preparation remain subject to the offline payment policy and machine safety conditions.

functional_requirements.name: Offline payment fallback
functional_requirements.description: Provide the specified fallback to offline card processing or cashless storage when network or external payment services fail; the permitted fallback and acceptance rules require stakeholder definition.
outputs: Offline payment outcome or unavailable payment indication
preconditions: The permitted offline mechanism and acceptance policy have been defined and configured.
postconditions: The order receives an explicit outcome under the approved offline policy.
A payment that has not been accepted is not represented as accepted.

functional_requirements.name: Waste disposal registration
functional_requirements.description: Allow an authenticated maintenance technician to register physical emptying of a selected liquid-waste or coffee-ground bin and reset its waste counter to zero.
outputs: Selected bin counter reset to zero
preconditions: The operator has administrative access.
The selected waste bin has been physically emptied.
postconditions: The selected bin counter is zero.
Other bin counters remain unchanged.
Waste alerts are recalculated from current levels; operation resumes only when applicable overflow and other safety checks pass.

non_functional_requirements.description: Process captured facial images entirely in memory and immediately discard them after mood inference; do not store them locally or transmit them to external servers.
non_functional_requirements.measurable_criterion: During a camera inference test, no captured facial image is written to persistent storage or emitted in network traffic; the inference image buffers are released or cleared immediately after the inference step completes, including failure paths.

non_functional_requirements.description: Restrict maintenance functions to authenticated maintenance personnel.
non_functional_requirements.measurable_criterion: Without valid maintenance authentication, attempts to access the dashboard or diagnostic logs and attempts to register ingredient refills or waste disposal are denied. After maintenance logout, replaying the previous session or signing in as a normal user does not restore administrative access; fresh maintenance authentication is required.

non_functional_requirements.description: Failure of network connectivity or an external service must not make basic local manual ordering unavailable. Unavailable external recommendation context must degrade locally available personalized recommendations for logged-in users rather than disabling them.
non_functional_requirements.measurable_criterion: With network connectivity disabled, and separately with weather and payment service failures injected, manual category browsing, recipe selection, and supported customization remain usable. Payment outcomes follow the defined offline policy. For a logged-in user, disabling the weather/external context service still produces recommendations from locally available profile, history, time and beverage data when the local recommendation calculation remains operational.

non_functional_requirements.description: Preserve the actual customization parameters in every completed transaction record.
non_functional_requirements.measurable_criterion: For each completed transaction in a test set covering supported customization parameters, the stored beverage and customization values match the executed order; no completed transaction in the test set lacks a record.

non_functional_requirements.description: Manual, saved-recipe and recommendation ordering paths must respect ingredient availability and bin-dependent overflow interlocks.
non_functional_requirements.measurable_criterion: For each enabled path, depleted or below-threshold required ingredients reject selection. An overflowing bin blocks or halts every recipe/operation that depends on it. A verified independent recipe may proceed only when all other checks pass. Missing or unverified dependency mappings do not permit exceptions. Test both affected and independent recipes for each bin.

non_functional_requirements.description: Provide an intuitive touchscreen interface for category browsing, nutritional inspection, and recipe customization.
Reflect recipe customization changes and machine error messages in real time on their respective interfaces.

assumptions.description: This third artifact combines the AI artifact and Assignment 2 according to the student review; it is not an independent elicitation or a statement that the ten-function prototype implements the full specification.

Numeric importance and effort values for the original thirteen backlog capabilities are retained exactly from Assignment 2. Must remains a scope label and does not replace numeric importance. New items have no invented numeric ranking or estimate.

The baseline estimate unit is undefined. Retained estimates refer to historical baseline scope and need reassessment for expanded capabilities. Usability/time measurement targets are also undefined; no numerical targets are invented.

A beverage catalogue, prices, supported parameter ranges, ingredient capacities, thresholds and nutritional data will be configured. Concrete values remain unspecified in the reviewed full-system artifact.
Order confirmation and a calculated payable amount are mandatory before payment. Detailed acceptance/capture, completion, cancellation and fault-recovery policies remain unresolved.

Personalized recommendations require login. Available local profile/history/time context supports degraded recommendations if external context fails. Unidentified ordering and transaction-linking behavior remains to be decided.

Ingredient maximum-counter reset assumes a physical full refill; waste reset to zero assumes physical emptying of the selected bin. Partial refills remain unresolved. All enabled ordering paths use ingredient and bin-dependent overflow guards.
Manual outage fallback does not authorize dispensing without accepted payment. Offline payment policy, cashless-storage meaning, limits and reconciliation require agreement.

The camera permission policy requires agreement. Camera mood analysis remains in scope and is separate from the rejected optional natural-language LLM. Captured facial images must never be persisted or transmitted.

Allowing verified bin-independent preparation during another bin overflow is a student-directed design modification to the specification statement about halting operations on overflow. Independence requires an explicit verified mapping; it is not assumed merely because a beverage lacks coffee.

open_questions.question: Username and personal PIN inputs and username uniqueness are fixed. What PIN complexity, username matching rules, card enrollment/revocation, user-session timeout and maintenance-session timeout apply? Profile logout and maintenance privilege revocation are required.
Can unidentified users order, and how should their completed transactions be recorded or later linked to a profile? Personalized recommendations require login.
Which drinks, categories, customization ranges, ingredient consumption rules, and nutritional data sources are supported? Does nutrition update after customization?

Confirmation and a calculated payable amount are required before payment, and beverage prices must be displayed. How are prices/customization charges calculated, when are payments accepted versus captured, what constitutes completion, and how do cancellation or preparation failures affect payment?
What does offline card processing/cashless storage mean here? Which methods work offline, which transactions may be accepted, and how are pending transactions reconciled when service returns?
What user notice, consent, or opt-out behavior is required for camera mood analysis? May derived mood values be retained, and what happens if the camera fails or cannot infer a mood?

Which weather location/provider, freshness limits, score calculation, highlighting rules and recommendation quality criteria apply? What local-context fallback is used for logged-in users with missing external inputs or limited history?

What ingredient thresholds, bin capacities, alert points, overflow detection rules and monitoring intervals apply? Which verified preparation operations depend on each bin, and can hardware safely isolate an overflowing bin? How are partial refills and safe resumption handled? Physical bin-emptying registration resets the selected counter to zero.

What are the required response-time limits for customization, recommendations, dashboard errors, alerts, and overflow halting, and what touchscreen usability tasks and success criteria should be tested?
Which administrative actions and remote diagnostic users are permitted, how is remote access authenticated, and which event fields, retention periods, and offline logging behavior are required?
What information must receipts contain, how long should QR receipt access remain valid, and how should QR or email delivery behave during an outage?

What unit applies to the retained baseline estimates and what does the numeric importance scale mean? How should expanded scopes be re-estimated, and which numeric importance and estimates should be assigned to new items?

excluded_scope.reason: The student excludes the optional feature from this reviewed scope because it is not mandatory. This does not remove contextual/mood recommendations or their privacy constraints.

review_decisions.resolution: Restore explicit username, personal PIN and username uniqueness; retain valid-authentication and rejection behavior.
review_decisions.student_justification: The LLM version omits the explicit username, personal PIN and username-uniqueness details from Assignment 2. These details should remain explicit requirements so that registration can be implemented and tested consistently.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep linked NFC/card login and explicit invalid-authentication outcome alongside username/PIN credentials.
review_decisions.student_justification: The LLM version adds NFC/card authentication and explicitly defines what happens when authentication fails. These additions make the login requirement more complete.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep viewing and maintaining personal preferences.
review_decisions.student_justification: Maintaining personal preference profiles is explicitly required by the system description. The LLM makes the viewing and maintenance operations explicit.

review_decisions.resolution: Reject the AI omission and restore ingredient-information display from baseline R4 across the menu requirement, story and backlog.
review_decisions.student_justification: Assignment 2 explicitly includes ingredient-information display, but the LLM version does not retain it. This omission should be rejected so users can inspect beverage ingredients before ordering.

review_decisions.resolution: Accepted: apply AI ingredient-threshold guards and payment/readiness/preparation coordination consistently across enabled ordering paths. Retain the separately decided order confirmation and bin-dependent overflow modifications.
review_decisions.student_justification: The expanded requirement is relevant because it clarifies that ingredient availability must be checked consistently across all ordering paths, not only during manual selection. This improves completeness and reduces the risk of invalid orders.
review_decisions.source: Student clarification in the conversation, applied to the comparison table.

review_decisions.resolution: Restore confirmation and calculated amount as explicit preconditions before payment.
review_decisions.student_justification: User confirmation and calculation of the payable amount should remain explicit preconditions before payment. They make the payment flow clearer and easier to test.

review_decisions.resolution: Accepted: record completed transactions with actual customization values, associate identified users with their history, and verify record accuracy using AI NFR-04.
review_decisions.student_justification: The system description explicitly requires recording every completed transaction, including beverage customization parameters. The LLM makes this requirement explicit, providing the history needed for personalized recommendations.
review_decisions.source: Student clarification in the conversation, applied to the comparison table.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep calculated scores and score-driven menu ordering/highlighting.
review_decisions.student_justification: Recommendation-based menu ordering and highlighting are explicitly mentioned in the system description. They should be included as functional requirements because they are expected system behavior.

review_decisions.resolution: Require login for personalized recommendations; missing external context degrades recommendations rather than disabling the local calculation.
review_decisions.student_justification: Login should remain mandatory for personalized recommendations because they use the identified user’s data. Unavailable external services should reduce the available recommendation context rather than disable the local recommendation calculation.

review_decisions.resolution: Reject omission of emptying registration/counter reset. Restore selected-bin reset to zero while retaining monitoring and alerts.
review_decisions.student_justification: Monitoring alone cannot register that a waste bin has been emptied. Disposal registration and resetting the selected bin counter to zero should therefore be retained so waste readings and future alerts remain accurate.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep bin-specific status, faults, dashboard messages, event logs and remote diagnostics.
review_decisions.student_justification: The expanded waste status, fault reporting, dashboard messages, event logs and remote diagnostics are useful and supported by the system description.

review_decisions.resolution: Block affected preparation; allow demonstrably bin-independent drinks only if safe. Record the deviation from the specification blanket halt statement and require verified dependencies.
review_decisions.student_justification: This is a proposed design change to the system description’s instruction to halt operations on overflow. Preparation that depends on an overflowing bin must stop. Other drinks may proceed only when verified to be independent of that bin and when all other safety checks pass; unknown dependencies must block preparation.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep manual outage fallback and policy-dependent offline payment; do not invent policy details.
review_decisions.student_justification: Manual ordering during outages and offline payment fallback are explicitly supported by the system description and improve resilience. The permitted offline payment policy still needs to be defined.

review_decisions.resolution: Exclude FR-23, FR-24, NFR-08, US-13 and PB-16 from the operative scope; remove their dependent open question.
review_decisions.student_justification: The LLM correctly identifies the optional local language-agent feature. I exclude it from the current scope because it is optional; this is a scope decision rather than a claim that the feature is absent from the system description.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep memory-only processing, no disk/network image storage/transmission and immediate disposal including failure paths.
review_decisions.student_justification: Facial images must be processed entirely in temporary memory, immediately discarded after inference, and neither saved to disk nor transmitted externally. The LLM makes these privacy constraints explicit, including failure paths.

review_decisions.resolution: Keep the constraints with undefined measurable criteria and retain OQ-09; do not invent timing or task-success targets.
review_decisions.student_justification: The usability and real-time performance requirements are supported by the system description. I accept these constraints while recording that measurable usability criteria and response-time targets remain undefined and must be agreed before acceptance testing.

review_decisions.resolution: Restore explicit beverage prices to the menu and story acceptance criteria.
review_decisions.student_justification: Users should be able to see beverage prices before ordering. Although price display is not explicitly stated in the system description, retaining it from Assignment 2 helps users make informed decisions.

review_decisions.resolution: Reject the AI omission and restore deletion of a user’s saved recipes, including its acceptance condition and demonstration.
review_decisions.student_justification: Recipe deletion is included in the Assignment 2 demonstration but omitted by the LLM. Although the system description does not explicitly require deletion, it is a useful part of managing saved recipes and should be retained.

review_decisions.resolution: Require revocation on maintenance logout; the next normal user and previous session cannot reuse admin privileges.
review_decisions.student_justification: The system description requires secure administrative access but does not explicitly define logout behavior. Administrative access must be revoked when the technician logs out so the next user cannot reuse it.

review_decisions.resolution: Restore exact baseline numeric importance and effort for thirteen original capabilities in PB-R01 through PB-R13; retain undefined units and do not aggregate grouped values or invent values for additions.
review_decisions.student_justification: The LLM version loses the numeric prioritization and effort information from Assignment 2. Retain those values for the corresponding backlog items to support ranking and planning, while recording that estimate units are undefined and expanded work needs reassessment.

review_decisions.resolution: Every revised backlog item links to its functional/non-functional requirements and records its source backlog IDs.
review_decisions.student_justification: Traceability clearly links backlog items to the requirements they implement, making the backlog easier to understand, verify and maintain.
